name: Ottoman Empire (Mehmed IV)

areaKm2.note: world_1650 Ottoman Empire polygons = 5,494,842 km2 on the sphere (incl. North African and Arabian claims). Crete (1669) and Podolia (1672) added after 1650. Mid discounts nominal desert hinterlands.

population.note: Sum of HYDE 1700 country values (OWID population.csv): Turkey 8.5M, Egypt 4.5M, Greater Syria and Iraq ~3.0M, Balkans ~4.9M, Ottoman Hungary ~1.0M, Crete, North African regencies ~3.0M, Hejaz ~0.5M = ~25M. The Military Revolution article (Parker) gives 18M for c. 1650 without the regencies. Vassals excluded.

urbanization.note: OWID urban share: Turkey 2.5% (1700), Egypt 3.3% (de Vries-type, low); Istanbul ~600,000 and Cairo ~250,000 imply a 5,000+ share near 8%.

activePersonnel.note: Standing salaried forces: kapikulu 70,296 in 1670 (Janissaries 39,470, kapikulu sipahi 14,070, other 16,756) and fortress guards ~25,000 plus ~10,000 other salaried provincial troops (Military of the Ottoman Empire, Ottoman Army Strength table). Janissary paper strength rose to 62,826 by 1687-88 (Janissary article, Agoston 2014). Mid ~110,000 effective incl. ~8,000 naval personnel. Kara Mustafa's 1683 field army was 90,000-170,000 incl. Tatar and Danubian vassals (Battle of Vienna article).

trainedReserves.note: Timariot sipahis 22,000 (50,000 with cebelu retainers, 1670 estimate, same table) plus provincial sekban/levend mercenary infantry raised by governors for the campaign (~20,000-40,000). Crimean Tatars (~20,000-40,000 at Vienna) excluded as a vassal force.

supportPersonnel.note: Other kapikulu corps (gunners, carriage drivers, armourers, miners) 16,756 in 1670, plus fleet personnel (~8,000 non-oarsmen: a typical mid-17th c. fleet had 5,300 fighters and 10,500 oarsmen, Ottoman Navy article after Katip Celebi).

mobilizationRatio.note: Total establishment ~155,000-200,000 (1670 table plus provincial levies) on ~24M = 0.7-0.9%; War of the Holy League emergency levies pushed toward 1.2-1.6%.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Janissaries ~40,000-45,000 effective (paper 47,233 in 1666-67 and 62,826 in 1687-88, Janissary article) plus ~25,000 salaried fortress-guard infantry (1670 table). Many registered janissaries were part-time artisans who did not campaign.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5 (era-typical) to 0.75 (among the era best). Evidence: matchlock muskets without bayonet; janissaries lagged Western linear infantry by the 1680s (Agoston ch. 7)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: corps diluted by artisan entrants; no drill for volley fire

count.note: Kapikulu sipahis 14,070 in 1670 (Military of the Ottoman Empire table).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: mail, lance, bow and pistols

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: household cavalry, declining discipline

count.note: Field and siege guns of Kara Mustafa's army at Vienna: the Ottomans had few heavy siege guns and relied on mining; estimates of the train range ~130-300 pieces, mostly light (Battle of Vienna article order of battle). Grade C.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: plentiful but heavy, poorly mobile field guns; few heavy siege guns brought to Vienna

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: standing topcu corps, falling behind Western gunnery

count.note: Galleys and the first sailing warships (kalyon programme began 1682): a typical mid-17th c. Ottoman fleet had 40 galleys and 6 maonas (Ottoman Navy article after Katip Celebi).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: galley fleet obsolete against Venetian and Western sailing ships of the line

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: experienced from the Cretan War, but losing seamanship edge

count.note: Educated guess: galliots, Black Sea and Danube flotillas (the Danube flotilla supported the Vienna campaign).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: era-typical small craft

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5. Evidence: Koprulu-era administration still mobilised large armies, but Kara Mustafa failed to guard the Kahlenberg and was routed by Sobieski (12 Sept 1683)

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5-0.75. Evidence: janissary corps identity strong but politicised; provincial levies and vassals broke at Vienna

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75. Evidence: recent victories at Candia (1669) and Kamianets (1672); collapse after Vienna

weapons.note: Anchor: 5 (1600: arquebus/musket, pike, field cannon). Evidence: matchlocks and field guns, no flintlock-bayonet or linear tactics; behind the 1683 Habsburg army

armor.note: Anchor: 4.7 between plate-and-mail and half-armor. Evidence: mail and lamellar for sipahis; janissaries unarmoured

ships.note: Anchor: 5 (galleons) reached only from 1682. Evidence: galley fleet plus first kalyon squadron

fortification.note: Anchor: 5 (trace italienne). Evidence: bastioned works at Candia and Uyvar; Ottoman sapping the best of the era

logistics.note: Anchor: 5 (magazines). Evidence: menzilhane road-stage depots, state grain requisition and camel/ox trains (Murphey, Ottoman Warfare ch. 4) let armies march 1,000+ km from Istanbul to Hungary each season

communications.note: Anchor: 4.7. Evidence: ulak relay couriers on the menzil network

isr.note: Anchor: ISR uses the same years as the anchor table (1600 -> 5, 1805 -> 6). Evidence: cavalry screens, spies and merchant reports only; no aerial or signal intelligence

air.note: No aircraft or military balloons before 1783/1794.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (2011 int$): Turkey 832 (1650), 897 (1700); Egypt and the Balkans similar. Mid 870 interpolated for 1683.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess: war years 1683-99 forced tax farming (malikane later) and debasement; peacetime low, wartime mid.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: as 1566; guild crafts in Istanbul, Bursa, Aleppo, Cairo.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: Egypt and the Danube basin fed Istanbul; generally self-sufficient.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.009-0.011 (mid 0.0095): in a pre-transition age structure (Wrigley and Schofield type, life expectancy ~30-35) males reaching 18 each year are about 0.9-1.1% of total population. Males only.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: Balkan military roads and Anatolian caravan network.

majorPorts.note: Istanbul arsenal, Gallipoli, Sinop, Izmir, Thessaloniki, Alexandria, Suez, Basra, Algiers, Tripoli, Candia, Rhodes.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess: Black Sea and Levantine coastal shipping; much foreign carriage (French, English, Dutch) by the 1680s.

supplyRangeKm.note: Murphey, Ottoman Warfare 1500-1700, ch. 4: menzil depots and Danube transport sustained a 1,200 km march Edirne-Vienna, but only for one campaign season.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: camels, horses, mules and oxen; pastoral sector large.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row in Anatolia and Rumelia; 1.1 on the Hungarian frontier.

notes: Snapshot = summer 1683, the Vienna campaign at the Ottoman territorial maximum (Podolia 1672). Population: directly administered provinces incl. the North African regencies; vassals excluded. Personnel convention: kapikulu, salaried fortress guards and naval personnel are active; timariots and governors' sekban/levend levies are trainedReserves; Crimean Tatars, Wallachian, Moldavian, Transylvanian and Hungarian Kuruc allies are excluded. Janissary numbers are pay-register paper strengths (Agoston 2014); the 1670 table row is the anchor. The siege army size (90,000-170,000) is disputed; the documents captured in Kara Mustafa's tent give 170,000 at campaign start incl. non-combatants and vassals.
